text: Engineer/Bicycle & Pedestrian Advisory Committee Chair

Growing up in Mountain View was the opportunity of a lifetime. I want a future where everyone can share in that opportunity. I have fought so that more kids can easily walk and bike to our schools and parks. I received a great education at our public schools, and have paid it forward by mentoring the Mountain View High School robotics team.

I will use my experience as chair of the Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee to efficiently deliver the projects that we need. I will make our bike lanes, sidewalks, and roads safer and more comfortable for everyone.

I am a renter who has spent years pushing the city to improve zoning codes, streamline permitting, and build affordable housing. I will fix outdated rules that make it unaffordable for those who work here or grew up here to live in Mountain View.

I have helped organize No Kings protests, and I will fight to protect the liberties of every resident, regardless of immigration status. I will always stand with the community that shows up for its neighbors, whether at food banks or at protests.
Vote James Kuszmaul for a better Mountain View for all. james4mv.com

text: Retired Software Engineer

I am your "Supporting Our Neighborhoods" candidate, a 17-year community leader and a 31-year Mountain View resident. I fought, and will continue to fight, for strong neighborhoods, thoughtful growth, more parks and open space, a thriving downtown and economy, and affordable housing. I offer practical environmental leadership. When new development has been proposed, I have worked to retain small businesses and parks. Above all, I want residents to determine the future of the neighborhoods in which they live. I oppose policies that will worsen traffic and parking issues.

On the Environmental Planning Commission, I recommended approval of over 4200 new residential units, 640 of which are affordable. On my neighborhood association board, I hosted over 20 neighborhood meetings, educating my neighbors on proposed developments. I have served in leadership positions in our local Sierra Club chapter, Mountain View Historical Association, and Kiwanis. I currently serve as Chair of the city's Rental Housing Committee and Chair of my neighborhood association. As a retired software technical lead and engineer who minored in economics, I understand the Silicon Valley economy. I am committed to supporting our quality of life and building Mountain View's bright future. I respectfully request your vote.
https://robertcoxforcouncil.com

text: Santa Clara County Commissioner, City Committee Member, Library Outreach Specialist

My name is Erik Poicon, I am running for Mountain View City Council to build a city where everyone can belong and thrive. I have served on the county Human Rights Commission and Mountain View's Human Relations Committee, and I work as a community outreach worker for our county libraries.

I understand how our city's decisions affect residents, how trust is earned, and how listening becomes action. I have experienced homelessness, relied on rental and food assistance, and helped neighbors access the same resources that once supported my family. On the Council, I will Champion affordability at every stage of life, including attainable childcare, strong youth programs, renter protections, senior housing, and diverse homes near transit. I will advance safer streets through Vision Zero, practical transportation choices, and improved accessibility. I will support workers, seniors, and small businesses in every neighborhood.
I will also expand neighborhood briefings, multilingual outreach, and accessible City Hall services so residents can shape decisions before they are made.
Mountain View needs leadership grounded in experience, service, and accountability. It needs decisions that let people stay, work, and build lives here. That is the work I will do for you on Council.

text: High School Teacher/Mother/Engineer

As a 43-year-old mom, science teacher, and engineer, I am running for City Council because I care about Mountain View. I love living here and am eager to make the city safer, greener, and more resilient in the face of climate change. My engineering background has equipped me with analytical tools needed to solve complex urban challenges. My daily work in the classroom keeps me grounded in the immediate needs of our diverse families and youth. Mountain View is a vibrant, growing community, and keeping it accessible and livable requires proactive, dedicated leadership.

I don't just advocate for our community; I take action to build it. I created the Pollinator Habitat in Cuesta Park and reinstated the Varsity Park Neighborhood Association. I will prioritize expanding safe infrastructure for our kids, building on our volunteer-led Bike Bus initiative at Bubb School, so all our residents can travel safely. My commitment is centered on building a stronger, more connected city for everyone. I will advocate for smart growth that balances urgent housing needs with environmental stewardship, fostering transparent governance responsive to every neighborhood. I am dedicated to keeping Mountain View safe, sustainable, and inclusive for every resident.
I would be honored to earn your vote.

text: Security Specialist

I was born and raised in Mountain View and proudly attended Slater Elementary School, Graham Middle School, and Mountain View High School. This city has always been my home, and I am grateful for the opportunities and sense of community it gave my family.

Growing up in a single-parent household, I watched my mother work tirelessly to make ends meet. Like many families, we faced challenges, but Mountain View gave us hope, opportunity, and a place where we could build a better future. When my mother passed away, it strengthened my commitment to give back to the community that gave so much to us. My career in security has taught me the importance of leadership, accountability, and making calm, thoughtful decisions during emergencies. Every day, I work to protect people, solve problems, and serve others with integrity.

If elected, I will focus on expanding affordable housing, improving public safety, supporting local businesses, strengthening community events that bring neighbors together, and promoting environmentally responsible policies that preserve what makes Mountain View special. I believe in listening first, leading with integrity, and making decisions that put our community first. It would be an honor to earn your trust and your vote.

text: U.S. Army Officer/Public Administrator

Living and working in Mountain View is a true privilege. It is one of the most innovative cities in the world. It is also clear from talking with neighbors in our city that most have the same burning question: can working families, young people, seniors, veterans, teachers, service workers, and small businesses still build a future here?
I'm running for city Council because I have the background and the commitment to help ensure that answer is yes.

My priorities are clear: expand workforce and affordable housing through practical public-private partnerships; support local jobs, apprenticeships, and career pathways; protect our parks and our environment; improve public transportation options and neighborhood safety, and ensure City Hall continues to serve its residents by remaining a welcoming community for all.

My background includes service as a U.S. Army Officer specializing in public policy, administration, and human relations, public sector experience up to the highest levels of government, and a lifelong commitment to community leadership. Most importantly, I believe in service before self and I have a hard-won experience bringing people together to solve difficult problems, both at home and abroad.
I respectfully ask for your vote. Together, let's build the Mountain View of tomorrow.

text: Engineer

Mountain View has been my home for 32 years. It's where I've been a long-term renter and first-time homeowner. It's where we raised our two kids. It's where I served our community on the city's Parks and Recreation Commission, Downtown Committee, Library Board, Environmental Planning Commission, and on a regional land use commission. My experience is broad and deep.
An engineer by training, I dive into analysis and listen to all voices to make thoughtful decisions. I'll bring this work ethic to the City Council.

I'm proud of our city and I believe we can make it even better by making smart choices. That means building affordable housing for our diverse community of families, seniors, and essential workers. It means expanding parks and tree canopy, especially in the neighborhoods that need them most. It means protecting the downtown we cherish and backing the small businesses that keep it thriving. It means confronting climate change today, with an eye on tomorrow. It means always maintaining a balanced budget.
Mountain View deserves thoughtful, experienced leadership. I've delivered that for decades and respectfully ask for your vote so I can continue to do so on the City Council.

text: Entrepreneur/Educator

I'm running for City Council to stand up for you, bring people together, turn ideas into action, and plan boldly for our future. For more than 25 years, I've worked to make Mountain View stronger, welcoming, and ready for new challenges. I've served on the Parks and Recreation Commission, Human Relations Commission, and Environmental Sustainability Task Force, as a volunteer City mediator, and in leadership roles with nonprofits supporting families, the environment, mental health, and our history.

During the pandemic, I founded Appetite for Good, saving dozens of restaurants while feeding hundreds of families. I built a coalition that advanced cleaner building standards across the Bay Area. I've also led pro-democracy events drawing tens of thousands of people together to protect our rights.

On Council, my priorities will be housing that enables people to stay and thrive, strong local businesses, thoughtful and effective leadership, safer and more connected neighborhoods, and a greener, more sustainable city. I listen deeply, find common ground, build consensus, and get things done. Together, we can meet today's needs and shape Mountain View's future with hope and confidence.
www.idarosesylvester.com
